siftei_kohen.he: ומאחר שעברו כו'. היינו לאפוקי אם הוא ידוע בודאי שלא עברו הימים אבל אם הבעל אינו יודע אם עברו או לא סומך עליה דכתיב וספרה לה לעצמה:
siftei_kohen.en: And since they have passed etc. That is to exclude if it is known with certainty that the days have not passed; but if the husband does not know whether they have passed or not — he relies on her, for it is written "and she shall count for herself."

turei_zahav.he: ומאחר שעברו כו'. קשה מאי קמ"ל דאח"כ דוקא נאמנת ובלא"ה אינה נאמנת פשיטא שאינה נאמנת כיון שא"א שטבלה בתוך אותו זמן ונראה שאפילו אם ספק לו אם עברו כ"כ ימים שאפשר שטבלה דהיינו שרגילה ללבוש לבנים ביום ו' לראייתה ועכשיו א"א בכך אלא שאם טבלה היתה צריכה ללבוש לבנים ביום ה' והיא אומרת שטבלה נאמנת כיון שעכ"פ אפשר בכך:
turei_zahav.en: And after sufficient days had passed, etc. This is difficult. What does this teach us by saying that specifically afterward she is believed, whereas otherwise she is not believed? It is obvious that she is not believed, since it was impossible for her to immerse within that period. It appears that even if he is uncertain whether enough days have passed for it to have been possible for her to immerse, she is believed. For example, she is accustomed to begin wearing white garments on the sixth day from the onset of her seeing, and under the present circumstances it would not have been possible for her to immerse unless she had begun wearing white garments on the fifth day. If she says that she immersed, she is believed, since it was at least possible for this to have occurred.

baer_heitev.he: שעברו. היינו לאפוקי אם הוא יודע בודאי שלא עברו הימים אבל אם הבעל אינו יודע אם עברו או לא סומך עליה דכתיב וספרה לה לעצמה. ש"ך:
baer_heitev.en: Passed. We would have been restrained if he knows that the days have not passed, but if the husband does not know whether he has passed or does not trust her by writing and telling herself. “Third:

beer_hagolah.he: ברייתא ספ"ק דנדה סוף דף י"א ודף י"ב:
beer_hagolah.en: B.B.B.B.B.D., The End of the Day of Hashem and the Holy One:

beur_hagra.he:
האשה כו'. י"א ב' י"ב א' ט"ז ב' ושם ט"ו ב' אבל ודאי ראתה כו':
ומאחר כו'. כתובות ע"ב א':
אפילו כו'. הרא"ש שם ותוס' שם ד"ה אי דלא כו':
beur_hagra.en:
The woman, etc. Niddah 11b, 12a, and 16b; and there 15b, 'but if she certainly saw,' etc.
And since, etc. Ketubot 72a.
Even, etc. The Rosh there and Tosafot there, s.v. 'if she did not,' etc.

pitchei_teshuva.he: טבלתי. ואפילו שוכבת אצלו לא מהני עד שתאמר לו בפירוש טבלתי. ח"ד:
pitchei_teshuva.en: I immersed. Even if she is lying beside him, this is insufficient until she explicitly tells him, "I immersed." Thus writes Chavat Da'at.

yad_avraham.he: (סי' קפ"ה סעיף א') האשה שהיא בחזקת טמאה אסור לו לבוא עליה כו'. עיין בבאה"ט בשם מהרי"ו הטוענת על בעלה ששכב עמה בנדותה והוא אומר להד"מ אין להאמינה. וכ"כ הרדב"ז ח"ג סימן ת"ז: **** ENGLISH **** (Siman 185 seif 1) Woman in presumption of tamei — forbidden for him to come on her, etc. See Baer Heitev in name of Mahari Weil claiming on husband he lay with her in her niddah and he says to her "to me you are not believed." Likewise Radbaz part 3 siman 407.
yad_avraham.en: (Siman 185 seif 1) Woman in presumption of tamei — forbidden for him to come on her, etc. See Baer Heitev in name of Mahari Weil claiming on husband he lay with her in her niddah and he says to her "to me you are not believed." Likewise Radbaz part 3 siman 407.

nekudot_hakesef.en: (K.A.) is difficult than May Camel. It’s not hard to have Dandadina been accused of practicing DNA, and the husband trusts it even from “shion” and it seems that even if he is doubtful that he is simply not interested in his difficulty and curse:

Imrei Moshe Hagazal s.k. 1 explained on Mahari Brandeis's question that we properly rely on double doubt even where possible to clarify by inquiry since veset is rabbinic — see there; his words fitting for one who said them to answer Mahari Brandeis's question on Shulchan Aruch; but still question in my eyes per Rif and Rambam and supporters as Ran wrote in Shevuot who hold like R. Yehuda vesetot are Scriptural and Beit Yosef brought this siman — then difficult what R. Yehuda said Niddah 15 doubt saw and doubt immersed — need not inquire — meaning need clarify; and with this no place for Imrei Moshe Hagazal's explanation; indeed as stated this law not clear regarding veset needing clarify initially — no question here; but per Shach who proved thus in general double doubt from Gemara — difficult; seems thus: nevertheless must understand in Gemara per Rif and Rambam who hold like R. Yehuda vesetot Scriptural — what we say there "say R. Yehuda in doubt saw there is double doubt certainly saw — who said doubt does not remove certainty" — initially difficult for R. Yehuda who holds veset — if so even examined and found pure — tamei for presumption she saw and we stone on presumption — likewise as certainly saw — what difference between saw etc.; nevertheless must say as stated although presumption of seeing nevertheless minority do not see as truly R. Zeira said if examined at veset time and found pure — pure; therefore lean this minority to presumption — presumption of purity at immersion time returns to prior presumption of purity and exists for majority unlike certainly saw no majority only presumption of purity of immersion establishes presumption against presumption and remains doubt and stringency — this is correct; therefore since majority against presumption of prohibition and also left her in presumption of purity from start before veset time — certainly strong no need even inquiry of meaning since she has presumption and majority against presumption — requires study; clear.

torat_hashlamim.he:
עד שתאמר לו טבלתי. ול"ד לדלעיל סי' קפ"ד סעיף י"א דא"צ לשאול אותה משום דהתם הוה ס"ס ספק אם ראתה ואת"ל ראתה אימור טבלה משא"כ כאן דודאי ראתה ואין ספק טבילה מוציא מידי ודאי כן הוא בש"ס בפ' כל היד אבל קשה לפמ"ש לעיל כלל נ"ט ס"ק ח' ובקונטרס הספיקות דאף דהיכא דאיכא ס"ס לא מתירין היכא שיש תקנה בשאלה א"כ אמאי מתירין לעיל אף בלא שאלה ואפשר דשאני התם דאיכא עוד חזקה שהייתי בחזקת טהורה וגם מסתמא דרכה לטבול ומ"מ היכא שהיא בחזקת טמאה לא סמכינן על זה מטעם דאין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי:
ומאחר שעברו ימים שאפשר לה למנות ולטבול נאמנת. ואם הבעל מסופק אם עברו או לא היא נאמנת ש"ך. וכ' הט"ז אפילו אם רגילה ללבוש לבנים ביום ו' לראייתה ועכשיו א"א בכך אלא שאם טבלה היתה צריכה ללבוש לבנים ביום ה' והיא אומרת שטבלה נאמנת:
torat_hashlamim.en:
Until she tells him, ‘I immersed.’ This is not comparable to the ruling above in siman 184, seif 11, where he need not ask her. There, there is a compound doubt: perhaps she did not see, and even if she did see, perhaps she immersed. Here, however, she certainly saw, and a doubtful immersion cannot remove a definite status. This is stated in the Gemara in Perek Kol HaYad. Yet this is difficult in light of what I wrote above in klal 59, seif katan 8, and in Kuntres HaSefeikot, that even where there is a compound doubt we do not permit the matter when it can be clarified by asking. Why, then, do we permit it above without asking? Perhaps that case is different because there is an additional presumption that she was previously pure, and ordinarily a woman immerses at the proper time. Nevertheless, where she has a definite status of impurity, we do not rely upon this, because a doubt cannot remove a definite status.
Once enough days have passed for her to count and immerse, she is believed. If the husband is uncertain whether enough days have passed, she is believed. Shach. The Taz writes that even if she ordinarily begins wearing white garments on the sixth day after seeing, and in this instance that would have been impossible unless she had begun on the fifth day, she is nevertheless believed when she says that she immersed.

chiddushei_hilkhot_niddah.he:
עד שתאמר לו טבלתי כיון דודאי ראתה אבל בספק אם ראתה מבואר לעיל דמחשב וסתה ובא עלי' דהוי ס"ס והקשה המ"י הא לא סמכינן אס"ס במקום שיש אפשר בשאלה ולק"מ דכאן אפילו ס"ס לא צריך דהא וסת דרבנן וספקא דרבנן לקולא רק אצטריך ספיקא אחריני דחז"ל עשוה כודאי רואה ולכך אצטרך ספיקא דטבילה כמ"ש דספיקא דטבילה מוצא מיד ספיקא דרואה ובזה לא תקנו חז"ל דין וסת וא"כ אין כאן ראי' מהא דצריך למשאל בדין תורה רק היתרה מכח ס"ס ואין לדמות איסורא דרבנן לשל תורה (עבק"א):
**** ENGLISH ****Until she tells him she immersed — since she certainly saw; but in doubt whether she saw, explained above we count her veset and he had relations — it is double doubt. Mahari Brandeis challenged: we do not rely on double doubt where inquiry is possible. Requires study: here even double doubt is not needed since veset is rabbinic and rabbinic doubt is lenient; only needs the other doubt that chazal made like certainly saw; therefore needs doubt of immersion — as written, doubt of immersion removes doubt of seeing immediately; through this chazal did not fix veset law; therefore no proof from here that Torah law requires inquiry — only leniency from double doubt; cannot compare rabbinic prohibition to Torah (Abraham Kapp).
chiddushei_hilkhot_niddah.en: Until she tells him she immersed — since she certainly saw; but in doubt whether she saw, explained above we count her veset and he had relations — it is double doubt. Mahari Brandeis challenged: we do not rely on double doubt where inquiry is possible. Requires study: here even double doubt is not needed since veset is rabbinic and rabbinic doubt is lenient; only needs the other doubt that chazal made like certainly saw; therefore needs doubt of immersion — as written, doubt of immersion removes doubt of seeing immediately; through this chazal did not fix veset law; therefore no proof from here that Torah law requires inquiry — only leniency from double doubt; cannot compare rabbinic prohibition to Torah (Abraham Kapp).
